title: Compact telemetry surface, modal stacking, and chart fallbacks for dashboards & cost pages
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: deliver a compact telemetry surface and resilient modal stacking behavior for dashboards, rollouts, and cost pages so the Console degrades gracefully across major browsers and lower-powered devices. This ticket scopes: 1) compact table density mode for telemetry and cost lists, 2) stacked modal behavior + keyboard focus rules when multiple modals/tooltips are open, 3) canvas-backed chart fallbacks for browsers that misrender WebGL/Canvas2D at high density, and 4) specific cross-browser remediation (Safari iOS/desktop, Edge with older Chromium flags, Firefox rendering anomalies). Includes prototypes in Figma and an experimental implementation branch for QA on BrowserStack.
acceptance_criteria: Compact mode toggle available on dashboards and cost views and preserves column affordances without horizontal scroll at 1280px width and above
Modal stacking: new z-index and inert rules prevent background interaction and maintain focus order for keyboard users; escape closes top modal only
Charts: canvas fallback renders identical data points and axis labels when GPU acceleration fails or when sequence lengths exceed sampling heuristics
Cross-browser tests: no visual regressions on latest stable Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge in canonical breakpoints (320, 768, 1024, 1366, 1920)
Performance: compact table rendering remains under 120ms first-paint on a mid-range CPU device (emulated), and chart fallbacks do not increase payload by more than 8%
Design sign-off from PM and Eng and linked implementation PR merged to staging branch
tasks: Create Figma compact-mode frames and token variants for dense row styles (font-size, line-height, token spacing)
Prototype modal stacking states with keyboard flows and accessibility notes in Figma
Document chart fallback rules (when to switch to rasterized canvas, sampling strategy) in the design spec
Pair with frontend to implement CSS variables for density mode and modal inert behavior
Run cross-browser visual regression suite on BrowserStack and collect failing snapshots
Iterate on fixes for Safari text subpixel shifts and Firefox table header sticky behavior
qa_plan: 1) Run visual diff across target breakpoints and browsers; 2) Execute keyboard-only modal flows and focus-trap assertions; 3) Validate compact table row density with synthetic datasets (200k tokens); 4) Verify chart raster fallback triggers at configured thresholds and matches numeric outputs from vector renderer; 5) Log any perf regressions and triage with frontend.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-offs discussed: 1) Aggressive density reduces discoverability; we keep a toggle to default to normal density for new users. 2) Canvas/raster fallbacks simplify cross-browser parity at the cost of reduced interactivity (hover tooltips implemented via overlay DOM layer). 3) Sticky headers vs virtualization: virtualization improves perf at extreme scale but complicates keyboard navigation; prioritize sticky header with row-level virtualization later if telemetry volumes require it.
